q: Management accounting is best described as the process of providing information primarily to:

options.A: Managers within the organisation for planning, controlling and decision-making
options.B: Shareholders for assessing past stewardship only
options.C: Tax authorities for assessment of income
options.D: Statutory auditors for certifying the annual accounts

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes management accounting from financial accounting?

options.A: Management accounting follows a format prescribed by law, financial accounting does not
options.B: Management accounting reports are prepared at intervals suited to management needs and have no legally prescribed format
options.C: Management accounting deals only with past data, financial accounting only with future data
options.D: Management accounting is compulsory for every organisation, financial accounting is optional

q: On Indian Railways, the Finance Officer acting as a management accountant helps line management most directly by:

options.A: Conducting the statutory audit of zonal accounts
options.B: Fixing the pay scales of railway staff
options.C: Supplying unit-cost, budgetary and operating-ratio information for decisions on services and expenditure
options.D: Maintaining only the cash book of the railway

q: Which of the following is a function of the management accountant?

options.A: Recording transactions only after the year ends
options.B: Auditing the accounts on behalf of the C&AG
options.C: Preparing the statutory balance sheet for shareholders
options.D: Interpreting accounting data and presenting it in a form useful for managerial decisions

q: The main purpose of standard costing as a control technique is to:

options.A: Fix the selling price of the product by law
options.B: Compare actual cost with a pre-set benchmark cost and analyse the variances for control action
options.C: Replace the financial accounts of the enterprise
options.D: Value the closing stock at market price

q: Standard cost differs from estimated cost in that a standard cost is:

options.A: Based on scientific and technical assessment of efficient operating conditions, whereas an estimated cost is based mainly on past experience
options.B: Always higher than the estimated cost
options.C: Prepared only after production is completed
options.D: Used only in financial accounting, not in cost accounting

q: For decision-making, management accounting information is distinctive because it:

options.A: Must always be expressed only in money terms
options.C: May combine monetary data with non-monetary data such as quantities, machine-hours and man-hours
options.D: Must be published for general public use

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A joint cost is incurred before the split-off point for products that are produced simultaneously from a common process.
2. A common cost is incurred for the benefit of several cost objects but does not arise from a simultaneous joint production process.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
In railway traffic costing, an example of arriving at fully distributed cost is:

options.A: Taking the total cost of a passenger service including its apportioned share of track, signalling and terminal costs
options.B: Taking only the fuel cost of running one additional train
options.C: Taking only the direct wages of the train crew
options.D: Ignoring all overheads of the railway

q: The salary of a divisional office that serves both the coaching and goods streams of traffic is, in costing terms, an example of a:

options.A: Direct cost of coaching traffic only
options.B: Common cost to be apportioned between the streams on an equitable basis
options.C: Marginal cost of goods traffic only

options.A: Contribution is sales minus total cost
options.B: Contribution is computed after deducting fixed costs
options.C: Profit is sales minus variable cost
options.D: Contribution first covers fixed costs, and only the excess of contribution over fixed costs is profit

q: The P/V ratio of a product can be improved by:

options.A: Increasing the selling price or reducing the variable cost per unit
options.B: Increasing the fixed costs of the factory
options.C: Reducing the selling price with no change in costs
options.D: Increasing the variable cost per unit

q: If the variable cost per unit increases while the selling price and fixed costs remain unchanged, the break-even point will:

options.B: Increase, because the contribution per unit falls

q: Under the materiality concept, an item deserves separate attention in management reports when:

options.A: It occurs every month without exception
options.B: It is recorded in the cash book
options.C: Its size or nature is such that omitting or misstating it could influence a managerial decision
options.D: It relates to the previous financial year

options.A: Every manager is charged with all costs of the organisation
options.B: Only fixed costs are reported to managers
options.C: Performance reports are prepared only at the end of the year
options.D: Costs and revenues are identified with responsibility centres, with controllable items shown separately from non-controllable items

q: An enterprise shows sales of Rs 6,00,000 with a profit of Rs 40,000 in one year and sales of Rs 8,00,000 with a profit of Rs 80,000 in the next year. The P/V ratio is:

options.A: Increases in direct proportion to output

q:
Consider the following statements about cost behaviour:
1. Variable cost per unit remains constant at different levels of output.
2. Total variable cost changes in direct proportion to output.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

A product sells for Rs 75 per unit with a variable cost of Rs 45 per unit. Fixed costs are Rs 1,80,000. The break-even sales value is:
A product sells for Rs 200 per unit with a variable cost of Rs 130 per unit. Its P/V ratio is:

options.C: Add Rs 32,000 to profit, so it should be accepted

q: The assumption that total fixed cost remains unchanged applies only:

options.B: For one accounting period only, in all situations
options.C: To variable costs and not to fixed costs
options.D: Within a given relevant range of activity and capacity

q: The variable cost is Rs 18 per unit. The total variable cost of producing 15,000 units is:
In a make-or-buy decision, the allocated general fixed overhead that will continue whether the component is made or bought should be:

options.A: Added in full to the cost of buying
options.B: Treated as irrelevant, since it is not avoidable and does not differ between the alternatives
options.C: Treated as a saving from buying
options.D: Added in full to the cost of making only

q: Total sales are Rs 15,00,000 and break-even sales are Rs 9,00,000, as in a unit whose P/V ratio is 40%. If fixed costs are Rs 3,60,000, the profit at the actual sales level is:
For pricing a short-run additional service, the most relevant cost concept is generally the:

options.A: Fully distributed cost including all apportioned overheads
options.B: Average cost of all services of the railway
options.D: Marginal cost of providing that additional service

q: As management accountant for a railway, providing a break-up of the cost of an uneconomic branch line service to help management decide on its continuance is an example of management accounting serving:

options.A: Decision-making with relevant cost information for a specific managerial problem
options.D: External audit of the branch line accounts

q: The prescribed test of remunerativeness of a railway work — a minimum return of 10% — is reckoned on:

options.A: The average capital employed over the life of the work
options.B: The initial estimated cost of the work
options.C: The gross earnings expected in the first year of operation
options.D: The total capital-at-charge of the railway

q: A proposed work is estimated to cost Rs 80 crore and is expected to yield net annual earnings of Rs 10.4 crore after meeting the additional working expenses. The anticipated rate of return, and the financial status of the work, are:

options.C: 13%; the work is remunerative, as it exceeds the prescribed 10% test
options.D: 10%; the work just meets the prescribed test

q: A proposed work is estimated to cost Rs 120 crore and is expected to yield net annual earnings of Rs 10.8 crore after meeting the additional working expenses. The anticipated rate of return, and the financial status of the work, are:

options.A: 9%; the work is unremunerative, as it falls short of the prescribed 10% test

q:
Consider the following statements about the Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) technique:
1. The earnings and expenditure streams of the work are projected over its life and discounted to their present value.
2. A rupee of earnings expected ten years hence is treated as equal in value to a rupee earned today.

options.A: The period after which it is receivable is shorter
options.B: The discount rate applied is higher
options.D: The sum is receivable in instalments

q: A machine costs Rs 8,40,000 and generates a net cash inflow of Rs 1,40,000 per year. Its payback period is:

options.A: A financial justification statement showing the anticipated rate of return on the estimated cost

options.A: The fare and freight earnings expected from the project
options.B: The capital cost of the project
options.C: The additional working expenses of operating the project

q: Where a project yields a uniform net cash inflow every year, its payback period is computed as:

options.A: Annual net cash inflow divided by the initial investment
options.B: Initial investment divided by the uniform annual net cash inflow
options.C: Initial investment divided by the average accounting profit
options.D: Total cash inflows over the life divided by the number of years

q: The Average Rate of Return method differs from the DCF methods in that it works with:

options.A: Cash flows discounted at the cut-off rate
options.B: Only the cash inflows of the first year
options.C: The salvage value of the asset alone
options.D: Accounting profit after depreciation, rather than cash flows

q: Projects X and Y have the same payback period, but X yields large cash inflows after the payback period while Y yields almost nothing thereafter. The payback method will:

options.B: Treat both projects as equally acceptable, taking no account of X's later inflows

options.A: Are not shown in the balance sheet

options.A: The enterprise depends heavily on creditors for finance

options.A: Profit before interest and tax is insufficient even to meet the interest charges

q: A steady fall in the inventory turnover ratio of an enterprise over the years generally indicates:

options.A: Peter A. Pyhrr at Texas Instruments

q: The first step in the Zero-Based Budgeting process is:

options.A: Ranking of decision packages in order of priority

options.C: Identification of decision units for which budgets are to be prepared

q: In traditional (incremental) budgeting, as distinct from Zero-Based Budgeting, the main focus of scrutiny is on:

options.A: Every existing activity from the zero base

q: A cash flow statement classifies cash flows under operating, investing and financing activities. A fund flow statement classifies movements as:

q: The Schedule of Changes in Working Capital that accompanies a fund flow statement shows:
